bull_bear.body:
- Leader in the export of two & three-wheeler tyres from India, with FY26 global sales growth well in excess of domestic sales growth
- Sustained market share in the domestic replacement market despite intense competition, and significant share achieved in the growing E-rickshaw segment
- Preferred supplier to ICE two- and three-wheeler OEMs, and assessed and cleared for supplies by a vast majority of the new clutch of EV two-wheeler OEMs
- Sustained R&D focus covering both new product development and fundamental material-science research, with design facilities in India and Italy
- Established just-in-time supply infrastructure for domestic OEMs plus a nationwide depot and distributor network for the aftermarket
- US channel presence acquired through Super Grip Corporation, integrated into the wider global outreach during FY26
- Renewable energy at approximately 90% of electricity at the Madurai plants and 100% biomass steam generation at the Uttarakhand plant
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Business concentration risk across products, market segments and geographies — The BRSR material-issues table and the MD&A risk summary both state that concentration has been in a few product and market segments and limited geographies, creating a risk of non-achievement of financial goals; the stated mitigation is diversifying the top line and aggressively seeking growth in global markets
- Raw material price volatility and inability to fully pass on input cost increases — Raw material costs represent a significant portion of the selling price and commodity price fluctuations have a direct correlation with profit margins; FY27 opened with an unprecedented increase in raw material prices largely driven by the Middle East conflict, and lower demand, stiff competition or inability to fully pass on cost increases affect earnings
- Globalisation risk - first and second order exposure to global events — The Indian economy's global linkages have risen so global events increasingly impact the Company directly, especially raw material costs; the Company's global revenue is rising at the same time as the global political and economic environment is becoming increasingly volatile
- Global economic conditions and supply chain disruption — Disturbances in the global economy could lead to supply chain disruption and thereby impact on-time delivery of raw materials; demand-supply mismatch and global economic policy changes can surge raw material prices and reduce the Company's contribution
- Organisation capability risk — Risk of not enhancing process and people capabilities to align with the short, medium and long term aspirations of the Company; mitigation is a competency framework, gap identification and plans to fill those gaps
- Export and geographic concentration exposure, including US tariffs — Exports contribute 19.69% of total turnover and the Company sells into 90+ countries; the MD&A notes a large part of FY26 was challenging for the US subsidiary Super Grip because of the tariff situation, and Indian tyre exports faced tariff restrictions
- Demand and end-market cyclicality including monsoon and macro shocks — FY26 saw a slow first half before a GST-cut-led recovery; management flags the uncertain effect of the Middle East conflict and a forecast poorer-than-normal monsoon likely to suppress rural demand as concerns for FY27
- Emerging technology and digitalisation risk, including Artificial Intelligence — The Company states it continues to review emerging risks arising from digitalisation and evolving technologies, including Artificial Intelligence, and has integrated these considerations into its enterprise risk management framework
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures two- and three-wheeler tyres and a range of pneumatic off-highway tyres addressing agricultural, commercial, industrial and materials-handling applications. Domestically it is a leading supplier of tyres to two- and three-wheeler OEMs as well as the replacement market, served through a network of depots, distributors and retailers. Its growing OHT business is focused on global markets, and its tyres are sold under the TVS Eurogrip, TVS Tyres, Eurogrip and Super Grip brands.

business.body:
- **Two & three-wheeler tyres:** TVS Eurogrip, TVS Tyres, Eurogrip
- **Off Highway Tyres (OHT):** Pneumatic tyres for agricultural, commercial, industrial and materials handling applications, Super Grip

outlook.body:
- Diversify the top line across product segments to reduce dependence on any single segment, and grow aggressively in global markets to mitigate geographic concentration
- Scale the OHT business as a global growth pathway, targeting an overall market opportunity stated as over US$ 20 billion
- Deepen the domestic aftermarket through structured programmes that increase width and depth of distribution, including actions to enhance brand position
- Build the global channel-partner network and place Company personnel in overseas markets to be closer to customers and more nimble by sub-segment
- Integrate the acquired Super Grip business in the USA into the wider global outreach
- Sustain R&D leadership across new product development and fundamental material-science research, using design facilities in India and Italy
- Enhance capacity in the two-wheeler and OHT segments through Board-approved investment in manufacturing capacity, productivity improvement and technology upgradation
- Build strategic procurement capability, use fungibility between alternate materials and finished-goods pricing to offset raw-material volatility
- Pursue a Sustainable Roadmap covering GHG emissions, carbon footprint and decarbonisation, moving towards close to 100% green electricity
- Develop a competency framework and fill identified capability gaps to address organisation capability risk
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was focused on productivity improvements to maximise utilisation of plant capacities already installed, while FY27 will see an enhancement in capacity in both the two-wheeler and the OHT segments through ongoing Board-approved investments in manufacturing capacity, productivity improvement and technology upgradation. During FY26 the Board approved additional capital expenditure of Rs 210.00 crores for the Uttarakhand Expansion Project at UKD-II, aimed at expanding the Company's manufacturing capacity. Subsequently, at its meeting held on 27th May 2026, the Board approved further capital expenditure of Rs 220.00 crores, comprising Rs 110.00 crores for the Two-Wheeler plant and Rs 110.00 crores for the Off-Highway Tyre plant, towards capacity expansion at the manufacturing facilities located at Vellaripatti, Madurai. Capital expenditure during FY26 itself amounted to Rs 106.09 crores. On the market side, the acquisition of Super Grip in the USA was integrated into the Company's larger global outreach during FY26, the global channel-partner network is being enhanced and Company personnel are being placed in global markets. On energy infrastructure, the Company completed a 5 MWp group-captive solar plant for Uttarakhand plant #1, uses 100% biomass fuel for steam generation at the Uttarakhand plant, and invested for a 5.92% equity stake in Navia Two Power Private Limited to purchase solar power under the Group Captive mode. The Company was granted a Structured Package of Assistance from SIPCOT comprising a capital subsidy aggregating Rs 75.00 crores receivable in 12 equal instalments, a Green Industry Incentive of Rs 1.00 crore and a training subsidy of Rs 68.40 lakhs. Manufacturing is carried out at Madurai in Tamil Nadu and Rudrapur in Uttarakhand, with design facilities in India and Italy.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian tyre demand grew about 6-8% in FY26 after about 4.4% growth in FY25, and tyre exports from India rose 9% in FY26 despite tariff restrictions
- The Indian auto industry saw a slow first half of FY26 followed by resurgence in the second half on the back of GST cuts, with the two-wheeler segment recovering close to pre-COVID levels
- Demand in FY27 continues to show strength as management writes, though the uncertain effect of the Middle East conflict and a forecast poorer-than-normal monsoon that could suppress rural demand are the stated concerns
- Global two-wheeler market valued at about US$ 120 billion in 2025 and expected to grow at a CAGR of over 6% over the next five years, with Asia Pacific about 70% of global sales and India the largest market and top exporter
- EVs already constitute about 20% of global two-wheeler sales and are expected to grow at a 30% CAGR over the next few years, supporting demand from EV OEMs the Company has been cleared to supply
- OHT segment presents an overall market size of over US$ 20 billion, the stated global growth pathway for the Company
- FY26 global business grew in both the two & three wheeler and OHT space, with annual growth of global sales well in excess of growth in domestic sales
- FY26 raw material costs moderated after a sharp rise from Q2 FY25, and strategic procurement plus in-plant waste reduction translated into improved profitability margins
- FY27 has opened with an unprecedented increase in raw material prices driven by the Middle East conflict, which management is mitigating through procurement actions, waste reduction and finished-goods price increases
- Management states that revenue itself does not present a challenge at least in the short term, given recovered market demand and the Company's expanded presence
- OECD projects global growth slowing from 3.4% in 2025 to 2.8% in 2026 before recovering to 3.1% in 2027 if energy prices ease, with India growth projected at 6.6% in FY27
- New products introduced at pace over the last two years, especially in OHT, moved into commercial production in FY26 and continue to receive excellent reviews in global markets
